meta.title: AeroStator Core — From idea to product, together
meta.description: Open-source (Apache-2.0) platform to design, simulate and prepare production of drive components built on AeroStator Core motors. For aviation and drones, robotics and marine. Connect your AI agents.

hero.title: From idea to product, together
hero.agents: Connect your AI agents and build together
hero.sub: Design, simulate and prepare production of drive components built on AeroStator Core motors.

concept.title: One platform, five steps
concept.sub: Inside: what you do. Outside: what is open to everyone.
concept.diagramAlt: Concept diagram. The AeroStator Core motor is in the centre. Five steps lead from idea to product: design, simulation, configure, 3D model, production. An outer ring shows the open ecosystem: open source, AI agents, community modules, your own compute.

steps.design: Set the motor geometry for your task.
steps.simulation: Electromagnetic, thermal and mechanical FEM, coupled.
steps.configure: Choose a motor for your operating point, cooling, propeller, battery and controller.
steps.model3d: Everyone can view the simplified model and download its STEP now. The full construction, tools and full STEP follow after NDA and account verification.
steps.production: Order motors from MOTRES or take a non-exclusive manufacturing licence.

sim.title: Simulation
sim.sub: One machine, three physics, one operating point.
sim.emAlt: Flux-density map of a permanent-magnet machine: the whole cross-section, twelve slots around ten magnets, coloured by |B| from 0 to 2.4 tesla, the finite-element mesh drawn over it, and the colour bar beside it.
sim.emHint: Flux density |B| of a permanent-magnet machine cross-section solved by 2-D FEM, with the FE mesh it was solved on. The solved half is repeated to the full ring, which is the periodicity the solve itself assumed.
sim.thermalAlt: Temperature map of the same whole cross-section, from 69 °C at the outer housing to 135 °C in the rotor, the finite-element mesh drawn over it, and the colour bar beside it.
sim.thermalHint: Temperature of the same machine with the FE mesh over it, coupled to the losses of the same run. The solved half is repeated to the full ring, as above.
sim.mechAlt: Deformation map of the same rotor under its retaining sleeve: the whole ring, sleeve, magnets and rotor iron, coloured by how far each point moves at speed, 7 to 146 micrometres, the finite-element mesh drawn over it, the colour bar beside it and the shape exaggerated so the bending is visible.
sim.mechHint: The rotor and its sleeve at speed with the FE mesh over them, coloured by displacement |u|. The shape is exaggerated 22 times so the bending can be seen.
